Package neqsim.thermo.util.mineral

Class ReservoirH2SEstimator

java.lang.Object
neqsim.thermo.util.mineral.ReservoirH2SEstimator
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class ReservoirH2SEstimator extends Object implements Serializable
Estimates the original (pre-souring) H2S content of a reservoir fluid from mineral buffering.

In clastic reservoirs that contain pyrite and an Fe-bearing carbonate (siderite or ankerite), the H2S fugacity is fixed by 4 FeS2 + CH4 + 3 CO2 + 6 H2O = 4 FeCO3 + 8 H2S, so that 8 ln f(H2S) = ln K(T,P) + ln f(CH4) + 3 ln f(CO2) + 6 ln a(H2O) - 4 ln a(FeCO3). The fugacities of CH4 and CO2 are taken from the equation of state of the fluid and the H2S mole fraction is solved so that its fugacity meets the buffer. The default Fe-carbonate activity of 0.38 reproduces the Haaland et al. (1999) correlation for Norwegian Continental Shelf sandstone reservoirs over 60-190 °C when applied to measured reservoir-fluid compositions with SRK.

The estimator also checks the phase rule: the buffer requires siderite to be stable relative to magnetite (CO2 fugacity above the siderite-magnetite boundary) and pyrite to be stable relative to pyrrhotite. Below about 70 °C the equilibrium is unlikely to be reached and bacterial sulfate reduction may dominate; carbonate reservoirs with anhydrite above about 120-140 °C may exceed the buffer by thermochemical sulfate reduction. Both cases are reported as warnings.

    • equilibrationTemperature

      public double equilibrationTemperature(SystemInterface fluid, double measuredH2SPpm, double lowTemperature, double highTemperature)
      Finds the temperature at which the buffered H2S of the fluid equals a measured value (H2S palaeothermometer).

      The buffered H2S rises monotonically with temperature at fixed composition and pressure. If the buffer equilibrated at an earlier, hotter burial stage and the reaction slowed on cooling, the measured H2S records that temperature; comparing the result with the present reservoir temperature gives the equilibration offset. The search uses bisection in temperature with the full equation-of-state buffer solution at each step.

      Parameters:
      fluid - reservoir fluid at its present pressure (its temperature is not used); not modified
      measuredH2SPpm - measured H2S in the reservoir fluid [ppm mol]
      lowTemperature - lower bound of the search [K]
      highTemperature - upper bound of the search [K]
      Returns:
      equilibration temperature [K], or Double.NaN if the measured value lies outside the buffered range between the bounds
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the measured value is not positive or the bounds are not increasing
